themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints spiked 344% last week (5 complaints vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), marking a statistically significant spike in public safety concerns in Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.18)
344% increase represents statistically significant spike with high severity classification
Signal appeared in last week's data, indicating emerging rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and local precinct about response to spike; map complaint locations to identify hotspots
Talk to residents and business owners about visible drug activity and safety impact; compare to prior year same period

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints jumped 269% last week (6 complaints vs. 1.6 weekly average), suggesting a localized environmental hazard or pollution event in Central Harlem that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 6 air quality complaints last week vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.41)
269% spike classified as high severity with statistically significant deviation
Last week timing indicates recent onset, not chronic baseline issue
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with DEP air quality monitors and EPA data; investigate industrial facilities, construction, or vehicular sources in district
Interview residents experiencing respiratory symptoms; contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection about source investigation

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped 256% last week (4 complaints vs. 1.1 weekly average), suggesting a potential public health outbreak or food safety violation pattern in Central Harlem restaurants or food vendors.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 3.68)
256% increase classified as high severity spike
Timing suggests emerging cluster rather than persistent issue
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene to identify if complaints point to specific establishment; request inspection records
Interview affected residents about which venues they patronized; check for common denominator (specific restaurant, food type, vendor)

themes_detail.label: Waste & Sanitation Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal and litter complaints accelerated significantly last week and 3 weeks ago respectively (9 disposal complaints last week vs. 2.6 avg; litter basket requests spike 1900% 3 weeks ago), indicating a mounting neighborhood sanitation crisis.
evidence: Residential disposal complaints: 9 last week vs. 2.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.26, up 243%)
Litter basket requests: 5 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 10.97, up 1900%)
Converging signals across two waste-related complaint types suggest systemic sanitation failure
reporting_angles: Inspect street conditions for overflowing trash, inadequate collection; request sanitation schedule data and staffing levels from DSNY
Interview residents about collection frequency and street cleanliness; identify specific blocks/intersections with worst conditions

themes_detail.label: Consumer Complaints Doubling
themes_detail.summary: Consumer complaints nearly doubled last week (14 complaints vs. 6.0 weekly average, up 133%), indicating potential business fraud, overcharging, or vendor misconduct escalating in Central Harlem.
evidence: 14 consumer complaints last week vs. 6.0 weekly average (z-score: 3.77, up 133%)
Spike classified as high severity on statistical measures
Last week timing indicates recent emergence
reporting_angles: Obtain detailed complaint data from 311 to identify business types and complaint categories; check with Department of Consumer Affairs for related enforcement
Interview residents about fraudulent practices they've encountered; identify if complaints cluster around specific businesses or industry sectors
